questions.stem: How does atherosclerosis lead to cardiovascular disease?

options.text: It makes red blood cells unable to carry oxygen
It causes the heart valves to become stiff and stop working
It weakens the walls of veins, causing them to leak
Fatty plaques build up in artery walls, narrowing the lumen and reducing blood flow

questions.explanation: Atherosclerosis involves the build-up of fatty deposits (plaques) inside artery walls. These plaques narrow the lumen, reducing blood flow. If a plaque ruptures, a blood clot can form and completely block the artery.
